items.title: What is built
items.text:
• Zenith fix (control.py prevent_windup): in eq mode the unwind check judges M1/M3 travel by the target's motor angles, not by the change in sky Az/Roll (on a wedge M1/M3 aren't the Az/Roll axes; near the zenith Az swings ~90 deg for a few deg of M1). Twin test test_goto_to_the_zenith_does_not_unwind.
  • utility/goto_response.py: a fixed sequence of 10 motor-angle gotos (⅖/30/90 deg on M1, 5/25 on M2, 5/30 on M3, 5 and ~30 on all three), each out from a base pose and back, with log_position on and each leg marked in the log. --track runs them while tracking, --plan checks the moves without moving, --twin dry-runs in the twin. M2 is kept within 5-70 deg and every target well inside the motor limits; Ctrl+C aborts.
  • utility/analyse_goto_response.ipynb (helpers in analyse_helpers.py): per run, leg and motor, the theoretical minimum time, arrival, commanded vs measured speed, response delay, overshoot, settling, and the Kd analysis below.
  • driver/control_plan.py (2026-10-17): the goto planning module (R3). GotoTrajectory, MotorTrajectory and ramp_rates moved out of control.py unchanged; min_move_time added. kinematics.theta_solutions lists every motor solution of a pose within the limits.
  • tests/test_control_plan.py: the twin sweep as a test, with the acceptance criteria as xfail tests (see the baseline).
  • Straight motor moves for idle slews over 15 deg (control_plan.MotorMove, choose_end_solution), and the LIMIT fix: see step 3.
  • utility/analyse_span.ipynb eq sections: reachability, PA (upright and upside down), the tripod (now the M3 disk model, R1) and latitude.
path: Goto Response — Theory, Measurements & Design for Flips, Unwinds and Goto Paths

items.title: What the measurements show
items.text:
Four runs on hardware, 2026-10-15 (logs/archive/alpaca.jdm_Beta8.0_10_15_Goto_Response_a1.log), level mode, coordinated speed control, default limits (planner at 0.8 Kv, Ka 5 deg/s², Kc 0.75'):

Run Mode, power Arrival - theoretical minimum (median) Overshoot (median) Tracking tolerance reached after 1' 1 idle, plugged in (draining: charging bug) 7.7 s 74' - 2 idle, battery 7.3 s 77' - 3 tracking, battery 8.9 s 1' small moves, 115-150' large +5.8 s 4 tracking, charging (59 -> 69%) 10.1 s 1' small moves, 115-190' large +6.4 s

Run 4's case 15 (m3_5_back) was stopped by hand and is left out.

  1. The motors follow their commands (measured / commanded speed 0.96-1.07 on large moves, all runs), whether one motor moves or all three: the independence assumption holds in these runs, on battery as well as charging.
  2. No measurable battery effect between runs, but the motors run faster than calibrated: M1 peaks at 10-11 deg/s against 8.92, M2 at 8-10 against 7.66 (the calibration underestimates by 10-25% at 49-69%). The battery % is unreliable around plugging in and out (the charging logic), so no conclusion on charge level.
  3. Idle gotos are planned but always overshoot: about 1-1.5 deg on every move, even 2 deg ones. The measured speed lags the command by 0.2-0.4 s (dead time, including the ~0.2 s age of a position sample); the plan doesn't allow for it, the motor falls 1-3 deg behind the plan, the PID pushes to full Kv, and the motor brakes late.

  4. Gotos while tracking aren't planned: the reference steps toward the target (up to 12 deg along the sky path, alpha_limit_step) and the PID chases it.

    • Small moves close as a first-order decay with τ ≈ 2 s: a 2 deg move that could take 1.3 s takes 12-13 s.
    • The Kd term sets that τ. With coordinated speed control ω_kd = -Kd (ω_fb - ω_ff) damps the PID's own feedback command back toward the feed-forward (the tracking rate), so ω_fb = Kp e / (1 + Kd): effective gain 1/(1 + Kd) (measured 0.65 and 0.57 on M1 and M3 against 0.67 and 0.56), time constant (1 + Kd)/Kp = 1.5 / 1.5 / 1.8 s, lengthened to ~2 s by the dead time and Ke smoothing. 5 deg to 1' is ln(300) τ ≈ 11 s.
    • Large single-motor moves reach full speed (the 12 deg lead) but have no braking plan: 2-3 deg overshoot.
    • Combined moves are slow because the lead is measured along the sky path: all_30 (M1 +30, M2 +25, M3 +30) is Az +84, Alt +12, Roll -47 in the sky; the 12 deg lead spread over three motors keeps each one's error, and so its speed, small (1-5 deg/s instead of ~8). 27 s for a move that could take 6 s.
    • Settling from 1' to the tracking tolerance (Kc/20 ≈ 2.3") takes another ~6 s, with BLC pushes in it.
    • A goto can complete while still moving: on m1_2_back (run 1) M1 passed through the target at ~0.5 deg/s, was within 0.75' for one tick, completed, went IDLE and coasted 11' past.
path: Goto Response — Theory, Measurements & Design for Flips, Unwinds and Goto Paths

items.title: Plan from here
items.text: See Design. In order of what they gain: plan gotos while tracking too; compensate the dead time; complete only once stopped; choose the end solution once per goto for both modes; then tune the final settle (Kc/20, BLC). Throughout: the requirements - no path into the tripod cone, gotos interruptible from a moving state, new code in control_plan.py / kinematics.py reusing what exists, with FAST speed calibration re-enabled, and planning that never blocks the 200 ms tick on a Pi Zero 2 W or N1505.
path: Goto Response — Theory, Measurements & Design for Flips, Unwinds and Goto Paths

items.title: Background
items.text:
How a goto's motor path is decided today:

  1. q_to_theta picks one of the two IK branches (normal, or flipped: M1 ±180, -M2, M3 ∓180), whichever is nearer LastPosition, with a gimbal lock fallback.
  2. plan_goto (coordinated speed control) follows a trajectory in sky space (Az/Alt when idle, RA/Dec/PA while tracking), giving up to the PID where the path needs a branch change; large moves while tracking aren't planned.
  3. prevent_windup runs, every tick and in this order, UNWIND (the implied raw angle past a limit: ±360), EQ ROOM (eq mode: M1 turned for tracking room), LOCK/FLIP (a path through gimbal lock: straight to the motor angles) and FLIP (the target > 30 deg away in M1 or M3: cache it).

Each heuristic estimates motor travel its own way, some from sky angles, and they can override one another mid-goto.
path: Goto Response — Theory, Measurements & Design for Flips, Unwinds and Goto Paths

items.title: Theory
items.text:
A pose has a small, finite set of motor solutions. M1-M2-M3 is a three-axis wrist: for one camera orientation there are two IK branches (normal, and flipped: M1 ±180, -M2, M3 ∓180), but with M2's range -8 to 81.5 deg both are valid only where |M2| ≤ 8 (the flipped branch needs -M2 in range too): outside that 16 deg slice by gimbal lock a pose has one branch. Each solution can also have M1 and M3 a whole turn either way. So the choice is almost always the M1/M3 turns, and the branch only in the slice. It is the same on a wedge: the wedge only changes the base -> sky rotation (alignQ_B2T), not the motors' geometry.

With independent motors the fastest move to a chosen solution is known exactly. If each motor has its own speed and acceleration limit and doesn't constrain the others (confirmed in the measurements above), the minimum time is the slowest single motor's rest-to-rest time (accelerate, cruise, decelerate). Nothing beats it, and a coordinated straight line in motor angles achieves it.

A straight motor-space move can't cross a motor limit: the limits form a box and a straight line between two points inside a box stays inside it. Gimbal lock is no obstacle to a motor-space move either; it's a singularity of the sky -> motor conversion, not of the motors.

So an ideal free move is a discrete choice of end solution, then a straight, time-optimal motor move to it.

Where that needs more:

  • Constrained paths: holding Az/Alt through a roll change, or RA/Dec through a PA change, can't be faster than a free move. Following a fixed path as fast as each motor's limits allow is time-optimal path following (Bobrow; Shin & McKay, 1985), which GotoTrajectory approximates. Constrain the path when what the camera sees during the move matters (a rotation on the same target, small corrections); slews between targets move freely.
  • A rotation must keep the pointing, or the pose is lost: M3 turns the camera about camera-up (the M3 axis), so M3 alone pans the boresight - a roll or PA change is never a single-motor move but M1, M2 and M3 together, and a straight motor-space move to the rotated pose swings the pointing far from the Az/Alt or RA/Dec on the way. Rotations (and the rotation part of a goto) follow the pointing-held path.
  • Constraints that aren't motor limits: eq mode's rig tilt, the camera or cables against the tripod, the Sun. These can rule out straight lines.
  • What else matters than speed: tracking room (below) and cable wrap (M1 and M3 turning the same way) decide between end solutions.
  • Dead time: with a 0.2-0.4 s delay between command and measured response, a controller chasing the measured position overshoots. Compare against the plan delayed by the dead time (or predict the motor forward), and brake that much earlier.

Tracking room: after a goto, tracking keeps turning the motors for hours (M1 at ~15 deg/h in eq mode; M1 and M3 in alt/az). The same pointing reached at M1 +200 or -160 tracks identically, but if tracking drives M1 upward the first leaves 60 deg (~4 h) before a 360 deg unwind mid-session and the second 420 deg. Choosing by tracking room is what EQ ROOM does for M1 in eq mode.
path: Goto Response — Theory, Measurements & Design for Flips, Unwinds and Goto Paths

items.title: Digital twin sweep (2026-10-15)
items.text:
600 seeded random gotos (start pose × target, level and eq mode, idle and tracking) in tests/sim_digital_twin.py, against the theoretical minimum (planner limits). T_best: the fastest valid end solution; T_chosen: the fastest move to the end solution the driver chose; T_arrived: within 1' to stay.

T_arrived / T_best (median, p90) Chose a slower end solution (> 2 s lost) Hard failures level, idle 1.58×, 2.94× 2 / 90 18 level, tracking 1.67×, 2.98× 9 / 116 18 eq, idle 1.82×, 3.46× 22 / 107 (up to 50 s) 39 eq, tracking 1.76×, 2.74× 23 / 131 (up to 50 s) 19

Hard failures: LIMIT, finishing > 1' off after an UNWIND, or M2 driven out of its range (eq idle: 15 / 150, M2 ending at 106-265 deg against its 81.5 deg stop). One UNWIND remapped M3 further past its soft limit (Remap t3 -66.9 to -426.9): the implied raw angle came from the change in sky roll, in level mode too.

  • From unwound starts (M1/M3 within ±120 deg) 20-26% of level gotos and 40-48% of eq gotos struggled.
  • Every goto lost ~10-12 s against the theory whatever its size: the slow arrival measured on hardware above (the twin's 0.35 s FAST lag matches the measured 0.4 s).
  • Speed and tracking room conflict: in eq tracking the fastest end solution would leave < 8 h of tracking in 24 / 131 gotos; the driver favours room (1 / 131 under 8 h). The scoring order is a decision, not a detail.
  • The twin's M3 is slower than the mount's (30 deg: 19 s against 11-12 s).

items.title: The sweep as a test: today's baseline (2026-10-17)
items.text:
tests/test_control_plan.py rebuilds the sweep (the 2026-10-15 harness was lost with its scratchpad): 10 seeded gotos per case in the suite, 150 per case with --runslow (-k report -s prints the table, GOTO_SWEEP_CSV=path saves every goto). The acceptance criteria are its tests, xfail until the redesign passes them. It differs from the first sweep, so the numbers aren't directly comparable: start poses spread over M1's whole range (motor angle -60 to 420), any requested roll, T_best at full Kv (the planner runs at 0.8 Kv, so even a perfect plan of today's design scores ≥ 1.25×), and arrived meaning within 2' when the driver reports the goto complete. The end solutions come from kinematics.theta_solutions, the move times from control_plan.min_move_time; kinematics/tick counts the control loop's and the planner's kinematics calls in one tick (R4: counted, not timed).

Arrived Arrival / best (median, p90) Chose > 2 s slower (room excuses) LIMIT Remapped mid-goto Missed, at the 45 s timeout Kinematics / tick (max) level, idle 102 / 150 2.10×, 3.02× 6 (0) 29 41 37 1379 level, tracking 138 / 150 2.59×, 4.74× 0 2 29 12 376 eq, idle 91 / 150 2.33×, 7.72× 29 (0) 48 75 45 1393 eq, tracking 131 / 150 3.11×, 7.81× 36 (32) 13 86 17 394
  • Most misses end at the fixed 45 s goto timeout, which marks the goto complete wherever the mount is (111 of 138). Traced: UNWIND remaps send M1 a full turn the long way, or past its limit (Remap t1 +415.4 to +775.4, M1 then heading for +775 against its +450), and the timeout ends it 9-160 deg off.
  • LIMIT: the motors pass their raw limits in 92 gotos. The twin has no hard stops, so M2 can swing on past its stop (to 117-180 deg in 20 level gotos: the "rig tilt" there is M2 itself).
  • Tripod cone: entered in 2 eq gotos. Rig tilt passed 100 deg in 92 eq idle and 69 eq tracking gotos.
  • Planning work: the first tick of an idle goto does ~1,380 kinematics calls (the 201-sample plan plus the 91-sample gimbal lock check, several calls each), a tracking goto's ~380; a normal tick does a handful. The provisional budget in the test is 40 per tick.
  • Room excuses: in eq tracking 32 of the 36 slower choices leave the best end solution short of a night's M1 room, as the first sweep found; the rest of the slower choices aren't excused.

items.title: Step 3: straight motor moves (2026-10-17)
items.text:
Idle gotos whose pointing moves more than 15 deg now go straight in motor angles (control_plan.MotorMove): each motor on its own closed-form time-optimal profile from its current angle and speed, the end solution chosen once at the start (choose_end_solution: within the limits, eq tracking room, no cable wrap on a flip, then the fastest), the reference the plan as the measurements should show it (see below) so the PID doesn't push against the lag, and the goto timeout extended by the planned time. Redirected mid-move, it re-plans from the current speeds. Flips past gimbal lock and EQ ROOM turns use the same MotorMove (MotorTrajectory is gone). Gotos while tracking, and idle ones of 15 deg or less, are unchanged so far.

Also fixed: LIMIT mode left the motors running at their last speed. control() sent no commands in LIMIT and no stop either (the mount still counted as moving): in the twin M2 swung on to 157 deg and M1 ran at full speed; on the mount that drives into the mechanical stop. Entering LIMIT now stops every motor, and they stay stopped until the alarm is acknowledged (test_guard_limit_stops_every_motor).

Arrived (baseline) Arrival / best, median (p90) LIMIT Remapped mid-goto (baseline) Rig tilt > 100 level, idle 114 (102) / 150 1.95× (2.86×) 31 1 (41) 0 (20, M2 run-away) level, tracking 138 (138) / 150 2.59× 2 29 (29) 0 eq, idle 106 (91) / 150 1.99× (2.91×, was 7.72×) 33 5 (75) 76 eq, tracking 132 (131) / 150 3.10× 13 86 (86) 60
  • Mid-goto remaps are gone from idle slews (41 -> 1, 75 -> 5), and with them the long tail (eq idle p90 7.7× -> 2.9×). Eq idle chooses a slower end solution in 26 gotos, 23 of them for M1's tracking room.
  • LIMIT is now mostly a speed-model problem. The twin, like the mount, runs M2 and M3 faster than the speed table the driver plans with (the twin uses M1's table for all three: 16% faster for M2). The feed-forward carries M2 ahead of the plan, the PID holds it ~1.3 deg ahead (the mismatch over its effective gain), and that much overshoot at the end trips LIMIT when the end solution sits at M2's 81.5 deg, 0.5 deg inside its stop. Fixes, in order: FAST speed calibration (R3) or a live speed estimate per motor (scale the feed-forward by measured / commanded speed), then braking short of a limit.
  • ~13 s still separates arrival from the best on gotos that arrive. Traced: the move itself runs to plan; the time goes in the final settle, where the PID closes the last 1-3 deg (the speed-model overshoot) with its ~2 s time constant down to the 0.75' tolerance. Same fix: a correct speed model removes the overshoot the settle closes.

Then: FAST calibration, the motor response model and arrival only once settled. All runs below with the twin's FAST calibration approved (GOTO_SWEEP_CALIBRATED=1).

  • FAST calibration (R3): speed_controller.fast_rate_units builds the FAST tables from approved speed tests, so the feed-forward runs each motor at the speed planned. Alone it didn't help: the overshoot that was left came from the lag.
  • Response model: MotorMove's reference is the plan delayed by pid_Kt and passed through a first-order lag pid_Kl, i.e. what the measurements should show. A pure delay left a·Kl²/2 of overshoot at every stop (0.3 deg at 5 deg/s² and 0.35 s). Twin fitted open loop: Kt 0.35 s, Kl 0.4 s (a straight move tracks its plan within 0.21 deg). Mount, fitted from the 10-15 goto-response log (41 moves, θ_pv against ω_op per axis with a free speed gain for the uncalibrated FAST table): the total is well determined and the split isn't. On velocity the residual is flat at 5.7-5.8% of peak speed along Kt + Kl = 0.3-0.35 s (best 0.3 + 0.05). On position the best is 0.25 s in all, but with 0.7 deg left over because the speed error varies with speed. pid_Kt 0.2 s + pid_Kl 0.15 s is on the ridge (5.8%) and is kept. The split matters little at the mount's lag: a·Kl²/2 is 0.06 deg at 0.15 s.
  • Stale feedback (bug): in IDLE nothing is sent, but the PID went on integrating omega_fb against the idle error. The next goto started with up to -5 deg/s of it on top of its plan, ~5 deg of unplanned travel and a 1.6 deg overshoot at the end. control() now zeroes omega_fb whenever it sends nothing.
  • Arrival while still moving (bug): a goto completed once every axis was within pid_Kc of its reference, by measurements that lag a moving motor. Two ways it stopped short: a motor still creeping on at a SLOW/PWM speed (0.4 deg/s commanded ~0.05: 13' short), and the KF overshooting the motor while braking (22' ahead at the stop, converging ~1.5' per sample, 6.5' out when it first read on target). The IDLE switch then stopped the motors where they were. Now the PID measures each motor's speed from successive theta_pv (unsmoothed: an average read ~0 as it crossed zero) and a goto stays in AUTO, and doesn't complete, until every motor has run within ARRIVED_MAX_RATE_DPS (0.03 deg/s) of its feed-forward for ARRIVED_SETTLED_MEAS (3) measurements in a row.
Calibrated twin Arrived Arrival − best, median LIMIT Missed > 2' level idle: delay 0.6 s only 127 / 150 13 s 0 23 level idle: delay 0.35 + lag 0.4, before the arrival fixes 101 / 150 11.1 s 0 49 level idle: delay 0.6 s only, with the fixes 149 / 150 13.2 s 0 1 level idle: delay 0.35 + lag 0.4, with the fixes 148 / 150 10.9 s 0 2 eq idle: delay 0.6 s only 130 / 150 4 20 eq idle: delay 0.35 + lag 0.4, with the fixes 144 / 150 14.3 s 5 6

Tracking cases are unchanged (not planned yet). The lag model before the fixes looked worse only because it ended moves without the overshoot that had kept the settle running until the KF caught up. The one new LIMIT (eq idle seed

1132) is the old prevent_windup FLIP path, not MotorMove. It chose an M1 target past the limit (+332 deg), which the committed code also chose (it missed by 31 deg at the timeout). Its motors now just start sooner. That goes with moving _flip_motor_angles onto choose_end_solution (step 5). The ~11 s left between arrival and best is still the final settle (design items 4 and 6).

Where the ~11 s goes (level idle, calibrated twin, median). Best 13.7 s; the plan at 0.8 Kv adds 2.6 s; the response tail (Kt + 3 Kl, 1.55 s on the twin, 0.65 s on the mount) 1.7 s; the settle after the move 5.5 s.

  • Twin MCU, FAST to SLOW (twin bug): after a FAST move the twin ignored SLOW commands until the lagged FAST speed had decayed below 1e-4 deg/s, so it was deaf to the PID's corrections for 2-3 s. The mount reverses on a SLOW correction ~0.6 s after a FAST move (10-15 log). Fixed in sim_polaris_mcu: the FAST residual eases off while SLOW acts at once. Sweep: tracking gotos 17.4 -> 13.2 s over best (level), 20.7 -> 17.5 s (eq); eq idle 14.3 -> 12.4 s.
  • The KF dominates what is left, on the mount too. kf_measure_noise gives the 518 positions a variance of 0.0032 deg² (σ 3.4') on M1, against 5e-5 of process noise: the filter integrates velocity and trusts position little (position gain ~0.15 per sample, τ ≈ 1.3 s). Every fast stop leaves its estimate off, and it converges slowly. On the mount (10-15 log, KFLOG θ_state - θ_meas) that's 25-80' at the end of a deceleration, taking ~3 s to converge, sometimes overshooting to the other side by 5-11'. The raw positions are far quieter: about 2" per sample on M1 and M2 and 5.6" on M3 (robust σ of second differences of θ_meas_raw while tracking; M3 includes its sample-and-hold steps). The PID's PV − SP after the KF tracks below 1". The PID chases the transient, and goto completion waits for it (or, before the settle rule, completed on it). In the twin, with the position variance ×0.1, median arrival − best goes 10.3 -> 7.4 s and the settle after the move 2.8 -> 0.4 s. Misses just over 2' (2.5-3.5', 11 gotos) are the KF still 2-3' off at completion (seed 1143: M1 2.2' off, 3.2' miss; ×0.1: 0.03' off, 0.5' miss). Retuning it also changes tracking and guiding: open question below.
  • Done: the KF trusts position more during a goto (kf_goto_noise_scale 0.1: the position terms of kf_measure_noise x0.1 while a goto or rotate is in progress; tracking and guiding keep today's tuning). Calibrated sweep, arrival − best median: level idle 10.6 -> 7.4 s (149/150 arrived), eq idle 12.4 -> 11.3 s (144/150). With the mount's measured 518 noise in the twin (0.0006 deg, 2.2"; NOISE_DEG default is 1e-4): level idle 10.8 -> 7.5 s (142 -> 149/150 arrived), eq idle 12.5 -> 11.2 s (141 -> 144/150). Gotos while tracking are unchanged (13.4 s level, 16.3 s eq) and complete normally on the TRACK tolerance (pid_Kc/20, 2.25"); after completion the true error stays at 1-5" with no creep in the twin. x0.03 matched x0.1 at this noise; x0.01 was slightly worse. test_goal_large_goto_while_tracking_completes_within_15s now passes. (An earlier run at 0.006 deg, from step-to-step differences that included the motion itself, overstated the noise 10x and showed tracking gotos timing out: not real.)

  • Step 4: gotos while tracking are planned (2026-10-16). One that isn't small (past SMALL_MOVE_DEG) or a roll/PA change is now a straight MotorMove too (_tracking_move), to the end solution for where the target will be when the move ends: planned once for its length, then aimed that far ahead. The tracking feed-forward is held off during it; a new target drops and re-plans it; when it ends, tracking and the PID close the rest. A sampled GotoTrajectory replan there cost ~1,800 kinematics calls a tick (R4); without it, settle is within 0.5 s. Calibrated sweep: level tracking 141 -> 145/150 arrived, arrival − best 13.4 -> 9.9 s, LIMIT 2 -> 0, remaps 29 -> 0; eq tracking 135 -> 149/150, 15.8 -> 12.2 s, LIMIT 14 -> 0, remaps 84 -> 1. Kinematics per tick 369/380 (was 376/394). The same at the mount's measured noise. The 5 level misses are targets past M2's 81.5 deg reach: the mount tracks the nearest reachable pose with a steady 3.8' M1 lag, because the feed-forward follows the target's sidereal motion, not the clipped pose's (open). Found on the way: alpha_limit_step near the zenith (Az and roll the same rotation) turned a few arcmin into a partial 90 deg roll step, M2 5 deg off while tracking, then FLIPs into LIMIT. Within one step as a whole pose it now returns the reference. Tracking restore without BLC now ends engaged and on target in ~10 s (tracking takes the slack up after the planned catch-up), against ~23 s with BLC: BLC's take-up now costs time here (open). The end solution chosen for eq tracking room is logged ("for tracking room, N s slower"). Then: small moves while tracking (dithers, re-centring; under SMALL_MOVE_DEG of motor travel) are straight MotorMoves too, on the current IK branch at SMALL_MOVE_RATE. The sampled GotoTrajectory they used cost ~1,375 kinematics calls in a tick. Every planned move while tracking now moves with the target: MotorMove(drift=...) adds the target's motor rates at the goal to the reference and the commands, in place of aiming ahead with the tracking held off (that made M1/M3 jump in one tick and wait). Fixes found on the way:

    • MotorMove.step commanded the plan's speed at one instant, so a move shorter than a tick (a 0.02 deg dither lasts 0.13 s) commanded nothing. It now commands the mean speed over a tick centred on that instant (the same on a ramp; a mean over the tick just past was half a tick late and cost 1.8 s on level idle gotos).
    • The old EQ ROOM and gimbal-lock checks in prevent_windup still ran during a planned move: a 0.02 deg dither in eq mode turned M1 a full 360 deg. A planned move marks both checked (the plan chose the end solution).
    • At SLOW speeds the twin takes a new speed on the MCU tick with no FAST lag, so small moves model the dead time only (0.1 deg: 7.1 -> 5.8 s).
    Tracking move (level, 20 seeds) 0.02 deg 0.1 deg 0.2 deg kinematics/tick sampled GotoTrajectory (before) 4.1 s 5.7 s 7.2 s 1,375 MotorMove with drift 5.2 s 6.3 s 7.2 s 11

    Most of a small move is the PID's final approach to the TRACK tolerance (2.25"). Below 0.02 deg the PID alone is 0.5 s quicker but costs 373 calls a tick (the room/lock checks), so small moves stay planned. Sweep: level/eq tracking arrival − best 9.5/12.1 s, kinematics per tick 10/26 (were 369/380), within R4's 40. Idle gotos unchanged (7.4/11.2 s). In eq mode a 0.2 deg move from a pose short of M1 tracking room still turns M1 360 deg (51 s): the room policy, as the old EQ ROOM did on a session's first goto. PA/roll changes while tracking stay on the sampled GotoTrajectory: they must hold the pointing while all three motors turn (M3 isn't the camera's roll axis), and a straight motor move drifts the pointing 13' (median, up to 145') over a 10 deg PA change (fine only to ~1 deg). Their cost came from the fixed 200 samples and the old gimbal-lock path check on top. Now the path is sampled per 0.5 deg of motor travel (at least 6, plus a few packed near each end for the speed-up and braking), and a planned path marks the lock check done. PA change cost per tick 1,383 -> 111 (1 deg) / 316 (10 deg), same time (12/14 s) and accuracy. R4 in milliseconds (this PC, a Ryzen 9 7950X; a Pi Zero 2 W runs Python ~20x slower): the worst tick per goto was 13 ms level idle and 34 ms eq idle (~260/700 ms on the Pi: past the 200 ms tick, as the field heartbeat lags showed), tracking gotos under 3 ms. The cost was GotoTrajectory's sampling and the gimbal-lock path check (90 samples, each rebuilding the slerp ends). Now the trajectory takes at most 24 samples (step() walks the exact path and caps each axis, the profile only shapes the speed) and both reuse the slerp ends; the lock check samples 24 points and refines the closest approach by golden-section search (same answer as 400 samples on 3,000 random paths). Worst tick 5.6 ms level idle / 9.7 ms eq idle (~110/200 ms on the Pi), kinematics per tick 129/225 (were 1,054/1,433); sweep results identical. Median worst tick per goto ~3 ms (the goto's first tick). The eq idle LIMITs were a branch mismatch (2026-10-16): the driver's LastPosition starts at (180, 45, 0) and is only updated from its own branch choices (the 518 quaternion is resolved through it). From a start at low M2 the other IK branch (M1 -180, M2 negated, M3 +180) was nearer, so theta_pv began on it while the motors were on the first. _theta_limits (from theta - zeta) was then 180 deg off on M1/M3, and the planner, and the old FLIP before it, drove M3 past its stop. It can happen on the mount when the driver starts with M2 low. seed_branch now starts LastPosition at the raw motor angles from the 517 (zeta + 180, 45, 0) before the first measurement is resolved (polaris and the twin). Sweep: eq idle 144 -> 150/150 arrived, LIMIT 5 -> 0, remaps 3 -> 0; eq tracking remaps 1 -> 0. No case has a LIMIT or a mid-goto remap now. The goto completion log says STOPPED AT A MOTOR LIMIT when it ends in LIMIT (it said on target, the error being zeroed there). R2, redirected gotos (redirect at 3 s, to 10 deg from the current pointing or anywhere; idle and tracking; 15 seeds each): all complete. A controlled path (15 deg or less) redirected at speed carried its path speed onto the new path's direction in motor space and stepped each motor's speed (M1 4.9 -> 0.6 deg/s in a tick, 24 deg/s^2). It now continues straight in motor angles from the motors' speeds; the biggest command step is 8 deg/s^2 (the planned 5 plus feedback) everywhere (test_guard_redirect_at_speed_keeps_every_motor_speed_continuous). Controlled paths past a motor limit: near the zenith a 14.9 deg goto needed M1 past its stop along the path, and the old UNWIND remapped it mid-goto (45 s, 95 deg off). A controlled path whose sampled motor angles leave the limits now goes straight to the chosen end solution (design item 2's fallback). Sweep: level idle 149 -> 150/150, remaps 1 -> 0. All four cases: LIMIT 0, mid-goto remaps 0, every miss in level tracking (5) a target past M2's reach. Field test, 2026-10-16 evening (level, tracking). Idle gotos 13.5-29 s, on target. Three failures, all reproduced in the twin and fixed:

    • Goto to Alt 0 while tracking never completed, oscillating: level Alt 0 is M2 = 0, gimbal lock. Tracking's feed-forward solved J^-1 exactly and demanded the roll the motors can't make there (M1/M3 counter-rotating at 2.4 deg/s), and the PID fought how reference and measurement split theta1 + theta3 (+1932" M1, -1802" M3). Now kinematics.theta_rates is a least-squares solve that drops singular values under 3.5% (|theta2| within ~2 deg), for tracking and PEC feed-forward, and within 1 deg of the lock M1 and M3 each get half the combined error. Twin: 45 s timeout -> on target in 14.6 s (test_guard_goto_to_alt_0_while_tracking_completes).
    • Rotator moves straight after a goto went straight in motor angles: a roll change was recognised only with the pointing under 0.5' from the measurement, and the mount was still settling (Backlash Compensation taking up slack): 17 deg off the target mid-roll. Now a pointing change under SMALL_MOVE_DEG and less than a quarter of the roll counts as a roll change.
    • Roll changes on the pointing-holding path still left the pointing ~60' off (205-417' before today): it scales with the speed (~9' per deg/s). M1 runs at its cap along a curve, and M3's sample-and-hold makes it read ~0.3 s later than M1/M2. Roll changes now run at ROLL_MOVE_RATE 1 deg/s, and the sampled trajectory's reference has the same response model as MotorMove (dead time + lag, M3 +0.3 s). Worst pointing error during the field sequence (roll -30, +30, -60, 0): 60-1065' -> 5-6'; rotation times about the same (~22 s), settling decides them (test_guard_roll_change_after_a_goto_keeps_the_pointing). PA 10 deg changes 14 -> 18 s.
    • Pilot's status showed no Flip/Unwind for planned moves (only the old theta_ref_cache ones): a MotorMove now carries FLIP CW/FLIP CCW (is_flip) or UNWIND (M1 or M3 turning > 180 deg) as the status.

    • A long move (47 s planned, 64.7 s) was forced: the roll -60 at Alt -30 left M3 at -236, and the next target needed +56 (-304 is past the limit). Open: leave M3 room as M1 gets it in eq mode. The ~17 s over plan is likely M3's FAST speed uncalibrated on this mount. Field test, 2026-10-16 later (b37052c5; level, eq toggled). Three more, reproduced in the twin and fixed:

    • Tracking at Alt 0 Az 180 never completed (goto TIMED OUT at 46 s with M2 15" behind, the rotate pending for good: fixed 2026-10-20, a rotate shares the goto timeout and logs ROTATE complete) and the pointing sank ~13"/s. Inside the gimbal lock q_to_theta held the M1/M3 split (M3 from zeta) but kept M2 from the exact solution, which tilts M3's axis about that split's M2 axis. On the held split it tilted the camera the wrong way: M2 followed the field rotation (roll the motors can't make there; ~12"/s at Az 180) and the pointing went down with it (22' in 2 min in the twin). Now M1/M2 are solved for the boresight with M3 held (kinematics._lock_pointing, Gauss-Newton); a reachable pose comes out unchanged. The lag also never cleared because the integral is frozen while a move is pending. Twin, the field sequence: never -> 19.8 s, pointing within 0.1' for 2 min (test_guard_tracking_at_gimbal_lock_keeps_the_pointing).

    • A roll change asked for during a goto timed out: eq mode keeps the PA, so a goto to Alt -30 arrived at roll ~60; a rotator move to 0 23 s later is ~78 s of roll change at Alt -30 (M1 at ROLL_MOVE_RATE, ~0.5 deg/s of roll), and controlled paths didn't extend the 45 s goto timeout as straight moves do: TIMED OUT at 60.6 s, 227" off. GotoTrajectory.duration (off its speed profile) now extends it (test_guard_roll_change_during_a_goto_completes_on_target). The pointing is 5-10' off during such a roll.

    • Eq mode on, but the mount went on as alt-az: turning eq on kept the 4 sync points taken level, and the refit stayed level (0.4 deg tilt). Changing eq mode now clears all sync points (user's choice), starts from the new base's seed (ideal wedge / level) and persists the empty list; the fitted M2 scale is kept, the same value sent again keeps the points (test_toggle_clears_the_sync_points). Open: roll changes at low altitude are slow (~0.5 deg/s of roll, a 60 deg change ~80 s); M3 room at the end of a move. Field test, 2026-10-17 morning (level). Four more, reproduced in the twin and fixed:

    • Roll changes too slow (a +45 roll at Alt 61 took 56 s at 1 deg/s). The pointing leaves the path by the motors' timing mismatch x speed. Measured against the planned path in the twin: M3 ran 0.27 s ahead of M1, two causes. (a) M3's FAST speed: uncalibrated it runs ~20% faster than commanded (the twin models the mount's M2/M3 as faster than the baseline table; calibrated=True removes it). (b) M3_HOLD_DELAY_S 0.3 was tuned with (a) in place; with it gone true M3 ran 0.1 s late: M3's measurement is only ~0.18 s behind (the KF's velocity takes up part of the 0.6 s hold), now 0.18. Worst pointing during a 45/90 deg roll, three poses: calibrated 4 deg/s 5-8' (21-30 s for +45), 8 deg/s 12-20'; uncalibrated 2 deg/s 16-21' (31-49 s), 4 deg/s 22-52'. So ROLL_MOVE_RATE 4 with M1/M3 FAST approved, ROLL_MOVE_RATE_UNCALIBRATED 2 otherwise (the idle roll goal, <= 30', holds uncalibrated at 2, not at 4). Tried, not kept: path following by time-shifting each motor's reference to the latest motor's lag: worse at every rate (the hold-back fights the PID).

    • A +90 roll at Alt 15 ended in LIMIT, 74' off: past the reachable roll (81 deg). The PA path ran towards the unreachable PA, and once its samples passed the reach the clip switched to the frame nearer level (-95 -> +81, a 175 deg jump): branch change, PID chase, M2 past its limit. Tracking paths now aim at the reachable PA (_reachable_delta): on target, worst 8.8' (test_guard_roll_past_the_reach_while_tracking_keeps_the_pointing).
    • A goto sent during the last one's final correction crept (pano panel 14 -> 12: 80 deg at 0.21 deg/s, timed out at Alt -31 of 35): retargeted onto the small correction path, which keeps SMALL_MOVE_RATE. A redirect moving the goal more than SMALL_MOVE_DEG is planned afresh (test_guard_goto_sent_during_a_small_correction_is_planned_afresh).
    • An Alt jog through M2 = 0 logged a FLIP (M2 at -3, inside the overlap): the jog holds Az and Roll, and through Alt 0 with any roll that pose needs M3 to swing 90 deg; at 9 deg/s the reference stepped over the lock zone and swung M1/M3 30-70 deg, which the legacy "> 30 deg from the reference" check called a FLIP. Within JOG_LOCK_DEG (|M2| < 6) Az/Alt jogs walk in motor angles, solving only for the boresight's motion (the roll follows), with M2 held to the reference range; jog feed-forward uses least squares everywhere (test_guard_alt_jog_through_gimbal_lock_does_not_flip). Left: with M3 ~ +-90 near the lock no motor moves the pointing in Alt, so that part of the jog is dropped (it doesn't move).
    • Also: tracking restore now runs on a reconnect too (==RECONNECT==), when the driver isn't tracking but its saved state says it was; tracking otherwise carries on through a comms loss. Roll speed limit removed (2026-10-17, user's call). Twin, worst pointing during a 45/90 deg roll at three poses: the previous controller (coordinated off) 180-530' and 19-45 s, two of six timed out; the planner at full speed 47-94' uncalibrated, 7-20' calibrated, 18-23 s for +45; at the 2/4 deg/s limits 16-21' / 5-8' but 31-49 / 22-30 s. The planner at full speed beats the previous controller on both, so roll changes run at full speed; the idle roll goals (<= 30') are xfail again. A +90 roll at Alt 61/30 still takes ~57-60 s at full speed (not the roll rate). Cable twist (2026-10-17, pano panel 41 -> 40). A flip left raw M1 at -180; the next goto had to turn M1 +274 (the short way passed its limit) and the fastest end solution turned M3 +44 with it: net twist (raw M1 + M3) +318. The other, 6 s slower, left -42; wraps_cables only judges flips, so neither counted. choose_end_solution now prefers end solutions within CABLE_TWIST_MAX_DEG 270 of net twist (180 undid eq mode's tracking-room turn, +204 at the zenith, by swinging M1 282 deg) (test_guard_goto_does_not_wind_the_cables). Cable twist near the limit (2026-10-19, slow BLC pose sweep). Below the horizon the flipped branch sits at +-270-287 of net twist (M3 near 180), so a 3 deg goto (+4-7) crossed the 270 and chose a 360 deg M3 unwind, 50-56 s slower (28 poses timed out). A move may now end up to CABLE_TWIST_SLACK_DEG 30 past the limit when it winds the cables no more than that further than they are, and any move winding them no more than CABLE_TWIST_CREEP_DEG 5 further is fine up to CABLE_TWIST_HARD_DEG 360: at +315 (Az 135 Alt -5) a 5' correction had turned M1 a full turn for 50 s (cable_twist_over; test_guard_small_correction_with_the_cables_already_wound_goes_the_short_way). The field case (0 -> +318 in one goto) is still turned away. M2 at its limit (2026-10-19). A goto while tracking aims at the reachable PA (_reachable_delta); its MotorMove compared that delta_goal with the PA asked for, 25 deg apart at M2's 81.5 deg, re-planned every tick and never ended, so tracking's feed-forward never resumed and a 3 deg goto at Alt 82 timed out. The move keeps the target asked for (delta_requested) (test_guard_goto_while_tracking_at_the_m2_limit_ends_its_move). M3's sample-and-hold in the KF (2026-10-19). The 518 M3 value refreshes every ~0.6 s. On the mount the roll goto hardware test read 97' of pointing wander (reported Az/Alt); the twin, which models the hold, gave 109' reported against 19' true camera wander: most of it was the estimate pulled back to the held value (the goto noise scale makes the KF follow 518 closely), and the fixed 0.18 s M3_HOLD_DELAY_S in the path reference compensated that. While M3 is commanded faster than KF_M3_AWARE_MIN_DPS 0.1 deg/s, KalmanFilter._m3_rows takes M3 only on a refresh (its rate across the refresh interval) and predicts it between; the delay goes. Twin rolls at 4 deg/s, five poses: reported 100-109' -> 17-41', true 19-23' -> 12-27' (better at three), same times. Every 518 at all speeds (tried first) made the legacy controller's tracking swing (north alt 15, 27" one seed) and a below-horizon 5' correction time out (tests/test_kalman_m3_hold.py). On the mount rolls look much smoother. Planner speed share 0.9 (2026-10-19, tried and reverted). GOTO_RATE_SHARE 0.8 -> 0.9 (~8 deg/s at Kv 8.9): calibrated sweep, 160 gotos, median 23.4 -> 21.4 s, p90 44.5 -> 41.2 s, arrivals/LIMIT/misses/remaps unchanged. But test_guard_goto_into_gimbal_lock_does_not_stutter[short] failed (M1 reversing 3 times), and on the mount a 3 deg/s Az jog overshot 101' after release (58' at 0.8; jog shaping caps at Kv x the share). Back to 0.8 for Beta 8; 0.9 needs separate goto and jog shares and the gimbal-lock reversals looked at. Open: a 30 deg PA change from a pose near M2's top (85.9 deg) is past the roll the motors reach there; _reachable_alpha clips it by moving the pointing far away (alt 24.5), the path needs a branch change, and the PID chase unwinds into LIMIT (with 200 samples too).
    • A correction MotorMove after the slew (tried, not kept) in place of the GotoTrajectory replan was 0.6 s slower: even a tiny move waits out the response tail. The replan isn't the R4 cost either: after a slew its first tick costs no more than the slew's (370 calls). The 1,381 is a goto of 15 deg or less planned from the start.

items.title: Design
items.text:
1. Choose the end solution once, at the start of the goto, for both modes. Make the target pose reachable (below), list its motor solutions (M1/M3 turns, and the second branch only when the target's |M2| ≤ 8), drop those outside the motor limits or (eq) past the rig tilt on the way; score the rest lexicographically: never a limit, then tracking room up to a night (8 h, both modes: project the target's sky motion), then the move time, with cable wrap (M1/M3 the same way) as a penalty. Fix the end angles for the goto; nothing re-decides mid-goto. This replaces UNWIND / EQ ROOM / LOCK / FLIP during a goto; prevent_windup stays as the guard while tracking.

  2. Plan every goto, tracking ones too: a time-optimal trajectory with feed-forward to where the target will be on arrival, then hand over to tracking. Removes the PID chase (τ ≈ 2 s) and the sky-path lead on combined moves. The path depends on how far the pointing moves (agreed 2026-10-17):

    • Pointing moves 15 deg or less (goto_controlled_path_deg, the angle between the two pointings) and every roll/PA-only change: a controlled pointing path. The pointing travels the great circle from start to target (RA/Dec while tracking), and roll/PA changes in proportion to progress along it, so the rotation never swings the pointing off that natural path (a straight motor move would: M3 alone pans the pointing). As fast as the motors allow along that path (path following, GotoTrajectory today). If the twin sweep shows these moves much slower than straight ones, allow the pointing a small corridor around the great circle (e.g. 1 deg or a few % of the move) for the motors to cut corners.
    • Pointing moves more than 15 deg: fast and straight in motor angles, closed-form per motor from the current state; the path through the sky isn't controlled. Path checks (tripod cone, rig tilt) apply here; a controlled path of 15 deg or less between targets above the horizon stays within 15 deg of them and can't reach the cone.
    • Fallback: a controlled path that needs an IK branch change or passes the motor limits goes straight instead.
    • Redirects mid-goto (R2) can switch between the two, both starting from the current motor speeds.
    • Compensate the dead time (0.2-0.4 s): feedback against the plan delayed by the dead time, braking that much earlier. Removes the ~1-1.5 deg overshoot.
    • Complete a goto only once the motors have stopped, not on one tick within tolerance.
    • Goto timeout from the planned time plus a margin, not a fixed 45 s.
    • Then tune the final settle: Kc/20 while tracking and BLC pushes, once the overshoot is gone.
path: Goto Response — Theory, Measurements & Design for Flips, Unwinds and Goto Paths

items.title: Requirements (2026-10-16)
items.text:
The design must also meet these three requirements.

R1. Tripod collision prevention.

Superseded 2026-10-17 (user's model). The tripod is not a cone round the boresight's nadir. The camera and OTA sit square to the M3 axis, so spinning M3 sweeps the OTA - front and rear - round a disk square to the M3 axis, set by M1 and M2 alone; on a wedge that disk can reach the tripod when M2 tilts the M3 axis towards the horizon (worst with the M2 axis across the meridian; with it in the meridian plane the disk passes down the side of the tripod). The tripod is the solid cone its legs span (spreader, tray, head between them), not three lines. Modelled in utility/analyse_span.ipynb (Tripod collision: the M3 disk: 3D rig, M1 x M2 / M3 x M2 maps, and a sky map of the rolls the tripod takes: Sydney, front 1.0 / rear 0.5 / legs 20 deg: ~10% of reachable Az/Alt/roll above the horizon, none clear round Alt 60-82, Az 150-195 - the rear; very sensitive to the rear length). The boresight cone below and the rig-tilt limit (rig_tilt_deg, limit_rig_tilt, eq_rig_tilt_limit, the R1 acceptance test) are removed from the driver; no tripod protection is enforced until the disk check is designed (needs the rig's measured rear length and leg splay). The original text follows for the record.

The tripod fills the cone around the nadir: altitude -81.5 to -90 deg, at any azimuth. On a level mount the motors can't reach it: M2's 81.5 deg limit holds the boresight within -81.5 to +81.5 deg altitude, so this mode is unaffected. A wedge tilts that range: M2's limit is now measured from the M1 axis (the pole), and the nadir comes within reach.

  • Which poses. The clearest description is in sky terms, by two directions of the pose:

    • boresight nadir distance: the angle from the nadir to where the lens points (= 90 + boresight altitude). The tripod cone is nadir distance < 8.5 deg (tripod_cone_deg, new; 8.5 is the level mount's own margin, so alt/az poses never trip it; set it larger from the rig's measured clearance for long lenses).
    • rig tilt: the angle of camera-up (the M3 axis) from the zenith. This is rig_tilt_deg and eq_rig_tilt_limit, which already exist (the rig hanging under the Polaris).

    These are separate constraints. Every pose in the tripod cone has a rig tilt of 81.5-98 deg (camera-up is roughly horizontal when the lens points down), so eq_rig_tilt_limit ≤ 81.5 would exclude the cone too, but at a cost of much of the PA range near the poles. The tripod cone is the narrow constraint that must always apply.

  • In motor terms (Sydney wedge, lat -33.9, computed from the driver's kinematics on a 5 deg grid): 0.46% of motor space points into the cone. Every such pose has |M2| ≥ ~25 deg and M1 + M3 within about ±40 deg of 180. Few end poses are lost, but a straight motor-angle move between two clear poses can pass through it.

  • What the planner must do. Every planned path, braking and interrupted paths included (R2), is checked for boresight nadir distance (and rig tilt) along its length, not only at its end. If a path enters the cone, the planner tries the other end solutions (item 1). If none is clear, it adds a waypoint around the cone. If no route is clear, the goto is refused with a warning; the planner never clips mid-move. A target inside the cone goes to the nearest pose on the cone's edge, as reachability does for other targets out of reach.
  • Tracking into the cone (a target setting below the tripod) stops at its edge, as at the motor limits.

R2. Fully interruptible gotos. A goto in progress can be redirected mid-flight: a new SlewTo/target, a sync, a tracking change, AbortSlew, or an orbital's moving setpoint.

  • Replan from the current state, not from rest. Each motor's position and velocity (the measured θ_pv and ω, and the commands still in flight during the dead time, i.e. the state predicted one dead time ahead) are the start of the new trajectory. A motor moving away from the new target first brakes within Ka, and that braking time and distance count in the plan.
  • The end solution is chosen again for the new target, scored from that moving state. An interruption is a new goto: "choose once" applies per goto, never mid-goto for the same target. Reversing a fast-moving M1 can cost more than a slightly worse solution in its direction of travel, and the scoring has to see that.
  • No step in the commands. The speed commands stay continuous across the replan (within Ka), and the dead-time compensation (item 3) carries over.
  • Abort is the same planner with "stop" as the target: a planned stop within Ka, not a hard stop. Afterwards the goto completes only once stopped (item 4).
  • GotoTrajectory already replans "from the current speed" on retarget (per path, not per motor); build on that rather than writing a new planner.

R3. Architecture consistency. Put new code where the existing modules say it belongs, reuse existing functions, and minimise duplication:

Concern Module Reuse / move Goto planning: end-solution choice, scoring, trajectories, path checks (R1), replanning (R2), timeout control_plan.py (new) move GotoTrajectory, MotorTrajectory, ramp_rates out of control.py; plan_goto stays the PID's hook and calls it Kinematics: IK solutions (both branches, M1/M3 turns), reachability, boresight nadir distance, rig tilt geometry kinematics.py extend q_to_theta / LastPosition, reachable_azaltroll, altitude_to_maxroll, theta_to_jacobian; move rig_tilt_deg here from control_eq.py Eq mode policy: wedge alignment, tracking room (rig tilt limiting removed 2026-10-17) control_eq.py wedge_alignQ_B2T, eq_theta1_with_room (as a scoring input) Motor speeds and accelerations (Kv, Ka, SLOW/FAST) speed_controller.py RateUnits, _speeds_at; the planner reads its limits from here, no second speed table Backlash, PEC control_backlash.py, control_pec.py / control_worm.py unchanged Twin and tests tests/sim_digital_twin.py, tests/test_control_plan.py (new) twin sweep as a test; existing test_goto_trajectory.py cases move with the trajectories
  • Before adding a function, search for an existing one (wrap180, angular_difference, calculate_angular_velocity, theta_to_jacobian, quaternion_difference ...). Any new module is reviewed for duplicates of existing code before it's committed.
  • Config keys follow the existing names and comments in config.toml (tripod_cone_deg beside eq_rig_tilt_limit).
  • Speed calibration, FAST commands only. CalibrationManager was marked deprecated when the coordinated speed controller came in, and RateUnits now uses only the baseline FAST points. The measurements show those underestimate the speed by 10-25% (M1 10-11 deg/s against 8.92), and a time-optimal plan is only as good as its Kv. Re-enable the SpeedTest calibration (moveaxis_speed_test, Pilot's Speed Calibration page) for the FAST speed units only (RAW 200-2500 per axis), and feed the approved points to RateUnits in place of the baseline. The SLOW levels keep the firmware table. The worm profile row stays as it is.

R4. Platform performance. The driver runs on Windows, macOS, Linux and Raspberry Pi OS. The minimum hardware is a Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W (4 × Cortex-A53 at 1 GHz, 512 MB) and an Intel N1505 mini PC. Goto planning must have minimal impact on the 200 ms control loop and speed controller on that hardware.

  • The current planner as a baseline (2026-10-17): all of its work happens in the goto's first tick, inside the asyncio loop that also runs the speed controller, the Polaris socket and Alpaca. Measured in the twin on a Ryzen 9 7950X (a fast desktop, so a lower bound):

    Idle goto Goto while tracking Normal tick (control_step_calculate) 0.3 ms 0.4 ms First tick of a goto 40 ms 10 ms Of which plan_goto (GotoTrajectory.start: 201 path samples, each a slerp + IK) 30-41 ms - (large moves not planned) Each later tick (GotoTrajectory.step) 0.2 ms 0.2 ms

    The same path is sampled twice at the start of a goto: prevent_windup's _path_passes_gimbal_lock (91 samples) and the planner (201). A Pi Zero 2 W runs Python an estimated 10-20× slower than this desktop (to be measured), which puts the first tick of an idle goto at 0.4-0.8 s: two to four whole ticks.

  • The field logs show it already. The Windows field PC (logs 2026-10-06 to 10-14) logs heartbeat lags (the 100 ms pulse late) of 0.2-0.8 s right after gotos and rotates, with plan_goto / prevent_windup / GotoTrajectory._interp in the stack. This is the likely cause of the pause seen when a new goto is issued. The longest lags (2-15 s) come with "CPU: 100%" and position updates 1-3 s late: the whole machine saturated (imaging and plate solving on the same PC), not planning. Even so, planning must not add to that.

  • Requirements:
    • Budget: a tick's planning work under 10% of the tick (20 ms) on the minimum hardware, with no single tick over 50 ms of planning. The control tick itself is unchanged.
    • Never block the tick for a plan. Plan in slices across ticks, or in a worker (asyncio.to_thread). Under the GIL a thread still competes for the CPU unless the work is in numpy, and a separate process costs memory a 512 MB Pi can't spare. Until the new plan is ready the mount keeps following the current trajectory, or brakes within Ka. The new plan starts from the state predicted for its handover tick (R2), so a plan taking one or two ticks costs no pause.
    • Do less work: closed-form trapezoid/triangle profiles per motor for straight motor-angle moves (Design item 2's slews: no path sampling at all). Path sampling only for the pointing-held paths (rotations, small corrections), with the samples shared by every check that needs them (gimbal lock, tripod cone R1, rig tilt, the trajectory), not one pass each.
    • Vectorised kinematics: IK/FK over an array of poses in one numpy call, in kinematics.py (R3), in place of one Quaternion per sample in Python.
    • Cross-platform: pure Python and numpy/scipy (already dependencies). No compiled extensions or OS-specific code in the planner (numba and the like don't install cleanly on a Pi Zero or every Windows Python).
    • Measure it: one log line per goto with the planning time and the number of ticks it spanned, so field logs show it alongside the heartbeat lags; a twin test that counts planning operations per goto, not wall time, so it is stable on any machine; a benchmark run on a Pi Zero 2 W and on the N1505 before release.
path: Goto Response — Theory, Measurements & Design for Flips, Unwinds and Goto Paths

items.title: Poses, reachability and what is left to choose
items.text:
Az/Alt/Roll is only how a pose is written, and it writes some poses twice and is singular at the zenith - hence the wrap and flip rules in reachable_azaltroll (kinematics.py). In the design a target becomes a camera orientation (quaternion) once, and the rules separate into:

  • Altitude over the top (vertoramas, poles): alt 120 at az is alt 60 at az + 180 with roll + 180 - the same orientation written differently. Nothing to choose: its motor solutions are the same.
  • Upside down (roll ± 180, the same footprint): not a choice. Camera-up is the M3 axis and M2 keeps it within 81.5 deg of the M1 axis (the zenith on a level base, the pole on a wedge); up and its opposite are 180 deg apart, so they can't both be inside that cone. Hence altitude_to_maxroll ≤ 81.5 deg and roll and roll ± 180 are never both reachable: reachability decides which one the frame gets, though M3 itself can turn fully.
  • Reachability (M2 and M3): the reachable poses are those with a motor solution inside the limits; altitude_to_maxroll's cos(roll) = cos(θ2max)/cos(alt) is that boundary written in sky angles. A target outside it goes to the nearest reachable pose with today's priority - pointing first, then roll (the zenith zone: directly below on the same azimuth) - in motor space, which also covers eq mode, where _reachable_alpha now goes through the base frame and back.
  • Continuity: a target tracked through the zenith zone keeps its side (test_zenith_transit.py) - choosing once and holding the solution, not re-choosing as the target moves.

So per goto the choices are the M1/M3 turns, the branch in the |M2| ≤ 8 slice, and the nearest reachable pose when the target is out of reach. Panorama panels are gotos like any other (the driver doesn't control their timing); the existing pano, reachability and zenith transit tests (test_pano_wrap.py, test_reachable_azaltroll.py, test_zenith_transit.py) define the behaviour to keep.
path: Goto Response — Theory, Measurements & Design for Flips, Unwinds and Goto Paths

items.title: Eq mode reachability, PA and upside-down frames (2026-10-17)
items.text:
From utility/analyse_span.ipynb (eq sections; vector maths checked against the driver's reachable_azaltroll, theta_to_q and q_to_theta). PA is the driver's: camera-up from the direction of the north celestial pole.

  • Motor reach on a wedge depends on Dec and PA only, not hour angle. The rule is the level mount's (camera-up within 81.5 deg of the M1 axis) with the M1 axis on the pole; tracking turns M1 about the pole and leaves camera-up's angle to it unchanged. So a target that is reachable at some PA stays reachable at that PA all night, as far as the motors go (the rig tilt limit and the tripod cone depend on hour angle).

  • Upright, camera-up must lean toward the visible pole: in the south, |PA| beyond about 98 deg at Dec 0. Upside down (PA + 180, the same footprint) covers the centre band, |PA| below about 82 deg. Neither works where camera-up would be within 8.5 deg of square to the pole (PA near ±90 at Dec 0); that gap widens toward the poles until nothing is left beyond |Dec| 81.5 (the polar caps):

    Dec Upright Upside down only Either 0 45% 45% 91% -45 43% 43% 86% -75 31% 31% 62% -85 0% 0% 0%

  • Allowing upside down exactly doubles the reachable PA, at every latitude and every rig tilt limit (sky above the horizon: 43% -> 87% with motor reach alone). A PA and its upside-down twin are never both reachable (camera-up and camera-down can't both be within 81.5 deg of the M1 axis, nor both within a tilt limit of the zenith), so the flip only ever adds PAs. This is the "upside down is not a choice" rule above, seen in eq terms: for any requested framing at most one of the two is reachable, and reachability decides which.

  • What the driver does today: reachable_azaltroll tries the upside-down frame first and clamps to the nearest reachable roll only if neither is reachable; eq mode applies it in the base frame (_reachable_alpha). With eq_rig_tilt_limit set, limit_rig_tilt then takes the smallest allowed PA turn, which can be a nearer edge than the flipped frame (see Open questions).

  • The rig tilt limit costs PA, most near the equator (where the M1 axis is nearly horizontal). Mean share of PA reachable over the sky above the horizon, upright / either way up:

    Latitude Motor reach alone Rig tilt ≤ 100 Rig tilt ≤ 81.5 5 43 / 86% 27 / 54% 20 / 40% 35 43 / 87% 35 / 70% 28 / 56% 70 43 / 87% 43 / 86% 38 / 75%

  • Tripod cone (R1): no end pose above the horizon is affected at any latitude. Straight motor-angle gotos between poses above 10 deg enter the cone in 0.9% of cases at Sydney, about 1.2% near the equator and none from about 50 deg latitude (the wedge nearly level). Every one first tips the rig past 81.5 deg, and those gotos swing M1 and M3 a long way (median 159 and 162 deg against 90 and 76 for all gotos). The rig tilt passes 100 deg partway through 43% of straight gotos, so with eq_rig_tilt_limit set the path check matters far more for the rig tilt than for the cone.
path: Goto Response — Theory, Measurements & Design for Flips, Unwinds and Goto Paths

items.title: Tracking in eq mode
items.text:
With QUEST's alignment matching the real wedge, tracking turns the pose about the true pole and the IK spreads it over all three motors: M1 at the sidereal rate, M2 and M3 correcting in proportion to the wedge's error (computed from the driver's kinematics, 4 h from reachable eq poses):

Wedge error M1 over 4 h M2 over 4 h M3 over 4 h Peak M2/M3 rate none 60.16 deg (sidereal) 0 0 0 0.5 deg 59.9-60.8 deg 4-25' 4-45' 4-14'/h 2 deg 59.0-62.6 deg 17-100' 16-182' 16-55'/h
  • M3 takes out the field rotation a misaligned wedge leaves, which a two-axis equatorial mount can't.
  • M2/M3 creep at ~0.1"/s, far below the slowest SLOW speed (~21"/s): start-stop pulses (the speed controller's PWM), reversing direction during a night, where backlash takes up (BLC).
  • Tracking room in eq mode is M1's: M2/M3 use a few degrees a night at most.
  • QUEST needs syncs spread over the sky to see the pole axis error (its test uses four); with fewer, tracking drifts at about the error × the sidereal rate.
path: Goto Response — Theory, Measurements & Design for Flips, Unwinds and Goto Paths

items.title: Orbitals
items.text:
Orbitals can be tracked (advanced_orbitals, tracking rates 1-3 in orbital2delta) but never stayed on target well at longer focal lengths. That is more a tracking than a goto problem, but the two meet:

  • How it works now: every tick the setpoint is the orbital's RA/Dec computed 2.5 s ahead. While the orbital is below 10 deg altitude the setpoint isn't updated and the mount tracks sidereal where it is; once it is above, the setpoint jumps to the orbital - an unplanned goto while tracking, chased by the PID (τ ≈ 2 s, overshoot on large moves), onto a target that keeps moving.
  • A moving target needs its velocity (and acceleration) in the feed-forward: a PID that closes errors with τ ≈ 2 s lags a target moving at rate v by about v × τ unless the feed-forward carries the motion. The fixed 2.5 s lead should match the loop's real lag instead - the measured dead time is 0.2-0.4 s - and at 1 deg/s every 0.1 s of mismatch is 6'. Done 2026-10-20 (orbital_lead_sec, default 0.3 s), after the mount led NORAD 45417 live.
  • PEC (worm feed-forward) and BLC have since addressed periodic error and backlash, two of the problems that made orbitals hard; what's left is the moving-target feed-forward, the dead time and planning the acquisition: a planned goto to where the orbital will be on arrival (design item 2), then tracking with its rate.
  • An orbital response test like goto_response.py could measure this without the sky: follow a recorded or synthetic pass (in the twin, then on the mount in daylight) and compare θ_sp with θ_pv.
path: Goto Response — Theory, Measurements & Design for Flips, Unwinds and Goto Paths

items.title: Acceptance criteria
items.text:
• Twin sweep (to become a test: a seeded subset in the suite, the full sweep marked slow): no LIMIT, no mid-goto remap, M2 never out of range, chosen end solution within 2 s of T_best except where tracking room decides, median arrival within 1.3× T_best.
  • Hardware, goto_response.py idle and --track: median arrival - theoretical minimum under 3 s; overshoot under 5' on moves ≤ 5 deg and under 15' on large ones; no completion while moving.
  • Tripod cone (R1): in the twin sweep (eq mode, several latitudes) no sample of any planned path, braking included, has a boresight nadir distance under tripod_cone_deg.
  • Interruption (R2): twin tests that redirect gotos at random times mid-flight show continuous speed commands (no step beyond Ka), no LIMIT, and arrival within 1.3× the T_best of a plan from the moving state.
  • Platform performance (R4): in the twin, no tick does more than its planning budget of operations (none over 50 ms equivalent on a Pi Zero 2 W); on a Pi Zero 2 W and the N1505, no heartbeat lag over 0.15 s from planning across a goto_response.py run.
  • The existing test suite passes, including the pano, reachability and zenith transit tests.
path: Goto Response — Theory, Measurements & Design for Flips, Unwinds and Goto Paths

items.title: Open questions
items.text:
• KF position trust (2026-10-16). Decided: trust position more only during gotos (kf_goto_noise_scale), done. Still open: check on the mount that 0.1 suits its real 518 noise (~2" per sample), and whether tracking itself would gain from less smoothing.

  • BLC through a planned reversal while pulse guiding (2026-10-19, nina01, RA 20.77h Dec +30.9, M2 73 deg). M3 turned at ~20:37; BLC latched it (20:36:52) and pushed it through its 288" slack at 20:38:23 and 20:41:11 while PHD2 guided, then gave up at 20:42:04 (more than 2 crossings): M3 barely moving at its turn, the guide pulses kept reversing it across the slack. Guiding went from 2.5-2.9" (20:30-20:36) to 6-12" with 35-38" RA jumps and 8-9 s of Dec pulses per 2 min. Not over at the give-up: M3 then crossed its slack uncompensated, Dec to +22" under up to 60" of pulses per 10 s, until it engaged at 20:43:20. M3's slack here looked like 350-400", not the 288" configured. Sync guiding too (2026-10-14 23:20, M2: given up in 68 s with no sync between), and every reversal is slow (15 to over 30 min to take the slack up; 4 of 9 compensated ones given up, none clean). Decided (2026-10-20): BLC no longer compensates tracking reversals; the guider takes the slack up and PEC pauses learning through it.

  • End-of-roll clunk (2026-10-19), not reproduced. Heard at the end of rolls with coordinated speed control (all three motors at different speeds; not with M1 alone). The protocol log shows motors leaving FAST while still moving (M1 at +2.04 deg/s when SLOW +5A took over, 16:06:54) and, as the shared SLOW level follows the fastest axis, reversals at level 5 (+5A/-5A, also by a lone pacer whose demand lies between two levels). Listening tests on nina01, one motor at a time: SLOW reversals loaded or dithering at level 5, slow reversals, FAST at 0.5 deg/s into an opposite SLOW, and full-speed ramps down at 5 deg/s² into -5A or -5B/+5B/-5B/+4B: one clunk in 13, with the same commands as three silent repeats. So the driver's commands alone don't decide it (gear position, MCU timing?). Tried and reverted: FAST glide (keep a braking axis in FAST while it would make another reverse at level 5: fewer level-5 reversals on the twin, clunk still heard). Next: capture with protocol logging on during ordinary rolls and note the time (and roll) of each clunk.

  • Tracking room: 8 h in both modes? Alt/az tracking turns M1 and M3 at rates that vary with the pointing, so its room needs the projected motor path, not a rate.

  • Battery: Kv from the baseline underestimates the speed at these charges. FAST calibration (R3) fixes the table; is it enough, or does it also need a live Kv (it shows in the measured speed of every FAST move) or a margin?
  • Dead-time compensation: the delay is ~0.2 s of sample age plus the MCU's FAST lag; is it stable enough to compensate as a constant?
  • BLC's share of the final settle while tracking: separate it with a run with BLC off.
  • The twin's M3 speed: recalibrate it from these runs.
  • Eq mode rig tilt and the tripod cone (R1): both are path constraints. How fine must the path sampling be, and is a waypoint around the cone enough or does it need a planned detour? What cone suits long lenses, and does the tripod's leg spread (not a full cone) matter?
  • Interrupting a goto (R2): how far ahead to predict the state (one dead time?), and how much replanning every tick an orbital's moving setpoint needs.
  • Eq mode with a single-point alignment: how much of the wedge's error it leaves, and the drift that follows.
  • Orbitals: the 2.5 s lead against the measured lag; acquiring an orbital as it rises past 10 deg as a planned goto.
  • A goto that also changes roll/PA over more than 15 deg: blended into the straight motor move (as now planned), or rotate along a controlled path at the end of the slew?
  • Platform performance (R4): the Pi Zero 2 W's real slowdown against the desktop for this code; slices across ticks or a worker thread (and how much of the planning numpy can hold without the GIL); the exact N1505 model to benchmark; whether the field PC's 100% CPU episodes need the driver to lower its own load, or to warn.
  • Out-of-reach PA with a rig tilt limit: limit_rig_tilt takes the smallest allowed PA turn, reachable_azaltroll the upside-down frame first. Should eq mode prefer the upside-down frame (the requested footprint exactly) over a nearer PA edge, as level mode does?
path: Goto Response — Theory, Measurements & Design for Flips, Unwinds and Goto Paths

items.title: PEC Drift — When to Learn, When to Apply
items.text:
Branch: feature/equatorial_mode (Oct 2026). Started from 2026-10-20 20:45, when PEC Drift Correction learnt PHD2's catch-up after guiding started before tracking as a -30"/min Dec drift, applied it for 20 min (-165"), and PHD2 spent those minutes pulsing it back. This study sets out which guide corrections PEC should learn from, which it should not (ignore cases), when the rate it has learnt is fit to apply (inhibit cases), how each case is detected for both sync guiding and pulse guiding, and the data that verifies the design.

Code: driver/control_pec.py (PecMixin, PecAxis, GuiderCalibrationDetector). Analysis: utility/analyse_tracking.ipynb section 3 (who corrected the drift), utility/analyse_sessions.ipynb.
path: PEC Drift — When to Learn, When to Apply

items.title: Terms
items.text:
• Drift: the slowly varying rate at which the sky moves against the mount after the worm feed-forward, per axis (RA, Dec). PEC learns it from the running total of guide corrections, y(t) = pulse guiding + sync guiding + PEC applied (correction_breakdown), as an EMA of the rate over pec_tau_sec (450 s).
  • Learn: fold a guide correction into the rate. Ignore = take the correction into the total (it really was a correction) but not into the rate, keep applying the rate already learnt, and restart the rate's differencing afterwards (PecAxis.hold). An ignore case says why a correction isn't evidence of drift; it can last for one correction (STEP) or for a span of them (REVERSAL, ACQUIRE).
  • Discard = drop the correction altogether, not even into the total (OUTLIER today). Kept for corrections that can't be real; dropping a real one leaves the total short by it from then on.
  • Apply: feed the learnt rate forward to the PID every tick. Inhibit = don't apply it (the axis's rate isn't trusted yet, or no longer). An inhibit case says why.
  • Reset: throw the model away (a new pointing). Not an ignore: nothing learnt before it is kept.

The two lists below are the names logged in PECLOG: inhibit (per axis, today) and, proposed, ignore (the ignore case, e.g. 'REVERSAL:M2', 'ACQUIRE'; it replaces today's paused, which carries only the motors of a reversal or slack crossing, e.g. 'M2' — the notebooks read both, for older logs).
path: PEC Drift — When to Learn, When to Apply

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
• R1 Learn only drift. A correction that measures anything else (a re-centre, a guider's deliberate move, a mechanical transient, a stale position) is ignored, whichever guider sent it.
  • R2 One design for sync and pulse guiding. Both reduce to y(t) per axis. Thresholds are rates (correction ÷ update interval) or are scaled by each axis's own update interval: a 5 min sync gap with a 60" residual and a 2 s pulse of 1" are the same 12"/min.
  • R3 Use what the driver knows. Events the driver sees exactly (tracking on, goto/rotate complete, a pulse it rejected, a motor reversal, BLC acting, stale 518 data) start an ignore case directly, without waiting for the signal.
  • R4 Judge bursts over time, not per update. A catch-up, a dither or a slack crossing spans many pulses; a rule that sees one update at a time either misses it or, after a few in a row, learns it.
  • R5 Bounded damage. Whatever the ignore cases miss moves the rate only so far per update (robust update), so one missed case can't fit -30"/min.
  • R6 Undo what was learnt in hindsight. A case recognised only after it started (a calibration on its 3rd pulse, a burst once it is clear) rolls the model back to where the case began.
  • R7 Don't hide real drift. A genuine change of drift (a flip, a new target, cable drag) is still learnt within about τ; corrections ignored on clean guiding cost little learning time.
  • R8 Apply only a trustworthy rate. The rate is applied once it rests on enough time and corrections, not merely enough corrections (3 pulses arrive in 4 s).
  • R9 Explain itself. Each ignore and inhibit is logged with its case name (PECLOG ignore, inhibit) and drawn by the analysis notebooks.
  • R10 Testable offline and closed loop. Every case has archived examples and a digital twin scenario.
path: PEC Drift — When to Learn, When to Apply

items.title: Detection design
items.text:
Three layers, applied per axis to y(t):

  1. Event gates (R3). The driver's events start ignore cases directly: ACQUIRE, CATCHUP, GAP, REVERSAL, SLACK, SLIP, BLC, STALL, NONSIDEREAL, WORMTEST, JOG. Each has a minimum time; release also needs the burst test to report the axis settled. Cheap and exact, and they cover the cases seen so far that matter most.
  2. Signal tests (R2, R4), all on rates scaled by the axis's own update interval:
    • burst test: the rate over a short window (3 updates or 30 s, whichever is longer) against the model's rate and its σ; one-sided and beyond kσ is BURST, and its "back within kσ" is the settled signal for every case that spans corrections;
    • saturation (PG): SATURATED;
    • calibration, per axis: CALIBRATEPHD2, CALIBRATECCD;
    • step and outlier, as rates: STEP, OUTLIER.
  3. Robust update (R5). Before each update's observed rate enters the EMA it is clipped to the model's rate ± kσ (Huber-style). A missed case can then move the rate by at most kσ x α per update; a real change of drift still gets through over a few updates (R7).

Rollback (R6): each ignore case that is recognised late snapshots the model at its start (as the calibration detector does today with run_start) and restores it when confirmed: CATCHUP from the first rejected pulse, BURST from its first update, CALIBRATE* from the run's start.

Logging (R9): PECLOG ignore (replacing paused) carries the case name and, for mechanical cases, the motor ('REVERSAL:M2', 'SLACK:M3'); inhibit per axis as today plus MIN_SPAN / UNCERTAIN / STALE. A ->> Polaris: PEC drift ignoring corrections (CATCHUP) / ... learning again line at each change (today: PEC drift learning paused / resumed). The notebook shades each case in section 3, reading ignore or, on older logs, paused.
path: PEC Drift — When to Learn, When to Apply
